A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoMa v2 and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched reliably across the substantial layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original dense-matching, relative-pose, SatAst, runtime, and predictive-covariance experiments, including supplementary benchmark construction and analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds visual-localization and RUBIK results, EMA and backbone ablations, and a prediction-perturbation experiment.

M1.justification: The documented coarse-matcher overlap-loss coefficient changes from 0.01 in v1 Equation (2) to 0.1 in v3 Section 3.2 and Equation (2). The architecture, refinement losses, covariance prediction, and EMA remain unchanged. Whether this revision reflects retraining or a documentation correction is unstated.

E1.justification: v3 adds visual localization on Map-free and InLoc, and evaluation on RUBIK's geometric challenges (Sections 4.2 and 4.7). Map-free previously supported training and dense-matching evaluation; NuScenes previously appeared only through a qualitative example. These additions substantially expand evaluated tasks and scenarios, while the training-data mixture remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Section 4.7 adds a numerical comparison with the previous DUSt3R RUBIK result, 54.8 versus RoMa v2's 57.3 success rate; v1 discussed DUSt3R only as prior work. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark comparisons is unchanged. Newly cited LoMa and RaCo are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include Map-free validation with DA3 metric depth, InLoc using HLoc, RUBIK success thresholds of 5 degrees rotation and 2 meters translation, controlled EMA/backbone comparisons, and quantile-based prediction perturbation. Existing pose and dense-matching resolutions, sampling procedures, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds downstream EMA ablations on MegaDepth-1500 and ScanNet-1500 (Table 9), DINOv2/DINOv3 coarse-matcher comparisons on WxBS and Hypersim (Table 10), and a perturbation test of the subpixel-accuracy explanation (Table 13). These substantially extend v1's existing EMA bias plots, linear-probe comparison, kernel ablation, and covariance analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Predictive covariance remains an existing model output; the new quantile mapping defines an experimental perturbation rather than uncertainty reporting for benchmark results.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Map-free localization precision/AUC of 73.3/89.6 for RoMa v2 versus 59.7/84.4 for RoMa, RUBIK success rates of 47.3/53.1/57.3 for RoMa/UFM/RoMa v2, and the new ablation and perturbation scores. Retained benchmark scores are unchanged. The additional cited UFM ScanNet row, 31.6/54.1, disappears, while its reproduced 31.3/54.1/72.0 row remains.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.9 introduces an explicit residual quantile transformation, Q_UFM(F_RoMa_v2(r)), in Equation (7), defining the new perturbation analysis. Existing covariance mathematics and supplementary derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about robust, precise, efficient dense matching, diverse training, and predictive covariance. New benchmark-specific findings support these contributions. Clarifying 'denser matches' as more correct matches does not materially redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 Table 9 explicitly connects EMA's downstream benefit to benchmarks requiring subpixel precision, extending v1's bias-reduction discussion. The existing interpretation of MegaDepth's precision requirements and limitations concerning WxBS modality changes and AerialMegaDepth sky artifacts remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies DA3 metric depth and the HLoc pipeline for the new localization experiments, describes the quantile perturbation procedure, and revises the documented matcher overlap-loss weight. Detailed architectural dimensions, dataset processing, augmentation, and covariance/RANSAC implementation information in the appendices are retained. Code availability is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to DA3, hierarchical localization, LoMa, and RaCo. LoMa modestly extends the sparse-matching discussion, RaCo expands acknowledgment of prior covariance-related work, and DA3/HLoc support the new localization experiments. Positioning relative to RoMa, UFM, and feed-forward reconstruction remains stable.

P1.justification: The text receives local grammatical corrections, terminology clarifications, and limited restructuring around new experimental subsections. Keywords and acknowledgements are added, author order changes, and the obsolete supplementary MegaDepth-table explanation is removed. Most existing narrative and appendix prose remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from two-column to single-column layout. v1 Figures 1/2 become v3 Figure 1, Figures 7/8 become Figure 6, and pose Tables 4/5 are merged. New experimental tables and a RUBIK column are added. The duplicate supplementary MegaDepth table is removed without losing its results.

improvement.justification: v1 shows EMA bias plots; v3 additionally measures downstream pose accuracy and tests the precision explanation through prediction perturbation. Localization and RUBIK evaluations also strengthen practical validation. These additions provide an incremental quality gain over v1's already broad evidence, although terse reporting of new protocols and the unexplained loss-weight revision limit reproducibility gains.
